title: Electron Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Electron course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: Which side creates desktop windows?
questions.explanation: Electron's main process manages desktop windows. A renderer shows the HTML page inside a window, like a browser tab.

questions.question: When is BrowserWindow created here?
questions.explanation: BrowserWindow creates a desktop window. Wait for app readiness before creating it, then load a local page.

questions.question: What can the renderer use for ordinary page interaction?
questions.explanation: The renderer can use normal HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript. It does not need Node access to show a button or change words.

questions.question: Why does this policy block inline scripts?
options: script-src allows local script files, not inline code
questions.explanation: A Content Security Policy limits where a page can load and run content. For a local app, start with only local resources and external script files.

questions.question: Where is the preload path configured?
questions.explanation: A preload script runs before the page and can expose a small API. Its file path belongs in the BrowserWindow options.

questions.question: What is exposed in this example?
options: Only a small object with the club name
questions.explanation: contextBridge can expose a chosen value to the renderer without sharing full Node tools. Keep the exposed surface small.

questions.question: What does the bridge let the page request?
questions.explanation: IPC lets the renderer ask the main process for an approved result. Expose one named function, not a general-purpose message sender.

questions.question: Why wrap the bridge call in try and catch?
options: It makes the version number secret
questions.explanation: A request through the bridge can reject. The renderer should show a useful message instead of leaving an unhandled error.

questions.question: Why restrict navigation in a local utility app?
options: To keep untrusted pages out of the privileged app window
questions.explanation: A local app window should not become an unrestricted browser for unknown content. Navigation can be blocked when the app only needs its bundled page.

questions.question: Why clear the reference on closed?
options: It no longer points to a usable open window
questions.explanation: The main process can keep a reference to its window and clear it when the window is closed. This helps manage the app lifecycle.

questions.question: What does the activate handler check first?
options: Whether there are any open windows
Whether the page has a heading
questions.explanation: Desktop platforms have different conventions after all windows close. Electron apps commonly keep running on macOS and recreate a window when activated.

questions.question: Why test the packaged app as well as development mode?
options: Packaging automatically proves every feature works
Bundled paths and permissions can differ
questions.explanation: A packaged desktop app can behave differently from the development folder. Test its files, permissions and error paths after packaging.
